memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Israel sent messengers to say to Sihon king of the Amorites: "Let us pass through your country. We will not turn aside into any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will travel along the King's Highway until we have passed through your territory." But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. He mustered his entire army and marched out into the wilderness against Israel. When he reached Jahaz, he fought with Israel. - Num 21:21-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Israel made a reasonable and peaceful request. They simply asked to pass through Sihon's land, promising to take nothing and to stay on the main road. It was a fair offer, made in good faith.

But Sihon refused. More than that, he gathered his whole army and marched out to attack. What began as a request for peaceful passage became a confrontation Israel had not sought. Sometimes we can do everything rightly and still meet opposition.

This is worth remembering when we face hostility we did not provoke. Not every conflict is our fault. There are times when, despite our best efforts at peace, others choose opposition. Scripture tells us to do what we can: as far as it depends on us, to live at peace with everyone (Rom 12:18). But the response of others is not ours to control.

When opposition comes though you have sought peace, do not be shaken. God is not caught off guard. He was with Israel on that road, and He is with you. In Christ we have a peace that the world cannot take away, even when the world stands against us (John 16:33). Entrust the outcome to Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you respond when you face opposition you did not cause?
2. Are you doing all you can to live at peace with others?
3. Where do you need to entrust an unfair situation to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to pursue peace as far as it depends on me. When opposition still comes, keep me trusting in the peace Jesus gives that the world cannot take away. Amen.
